description: Returns the lines of a file as a lazily read `IEnumerable<string>`, so processing can start before the whole file is loaded, unlike `File.ReadAllLines`.
Methods such as `decimal.TryParse` return `false` for invalid input and write the value to an `out` parameter, so validation needs no exceptions.
`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` fixes the decimal point and number format, so parsing and output do not depend on the machine's regional settings.
The 128-bit base-10 numeric type used for money, which represents values such as `0.10` exactly where `double` cannot.
Output that is identical for the same input on every run and machine, which needs explicit tie-breaking in sorts and culture-independent formatting.
The integer a console app returns to the shell, `0` for success and non-zero for failure, which scripts and CI read through `$?`.
